html:
Iranian-speaking horse nomads who ruled the steppes north of the Black Sea and the Caucasus from about the 3rd century BCE to the 4th century CE. The map shows them in 100 BCE.

They came from the steppe between the Don and the Urals, where Herodotus placed the Sauromatians and told a story that they descended from Scythian men and Amazons. Graves of armed women in the region give the legend some ground. From the 3rd century BCE they pushed west and replaced the Scythians as masters of the Pontic steppe.

They were split into tribes such as the Iazyges, who settled on the Hungarian plain, the Roxolani on the lower Danube and the Alans further east. They were known for heavy cavalry in scale armour, forerunners of later cataphracts. They raided Rome and served it by turns; after a war with Marcus Aurelius, thousands of Iazyges were sent to serve in Britain. The Goths and then the Huns broke their power, though the Alans lived on, among them the Caucasian Alans.
sum: Iranian-speaking horse nomads who ruled the steppes north of the Black Sea and the Caucasus from about the 3rd century BCE to the 4th century CE. The map shows them in 100 BCE.
